newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on optimism for economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on optimism for economic growth.

text.p: Shares on Lima stock exchange closed up Wednesday as investors bought equities in the hope that recent figures signaling healthy economic growth this quarter would lead to strong company profits, brokers said.
But in the wake of recent gains, players expect a technical correction Thursday, the brokers added.

Wednesday, the General Index rose 0.30 percent to 1,578.8 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.39 percent to 2,268.0 points. In a total of 1,819 trades, 35 stocks remained unchanged, 31 rose and 26 fell.
"I think the market is strong because the medium- and long-term prospects are promising," said Luis Calderon of local brokerage Acciones y Valores.

Telefonica del Peru dominated Wednesday's session as a flood of foreign investors sought to buy the benchmark stock. Telefonica climbed 0.51 percent to 5.91 soles with 38 percent of the day's total trade.
The country's leader in financial services, Holding Credicorp, was the second most heavily traded stock as it rose 1.55 percent to $21.60 with 10 percent of the day's trade.
